driver: The decisive move is recovering the entity the governing rule pays from records kept at a registry identifier, by matching each unit that ceased to the unit that opened the next day with an identical set of attached sub-units, which lets those entities pass a continuous-filing gate and reverses the downward corrections into a higher total.
driver_concrete: Rule 3 pays the firm while the register keys the NZBN, so the 203 units that ceased and the 203 that opened the next day filing the identical site set are one firm each, letting 119 firms worth NZD 3,024,200 clear rule 4's every-month gate and lifting the run from NZD 4,701,600 to NZD 7,725,800.
stump: A competent solver nets each register unit's PAYE registrations at the amended schedule, back-tests the pilot to the dollar and files NZD 4,701,600 across 352 units, because it groups by the NZBN and never links the 203 units that ceased and reopened the next day on identical site sets, so rule 4 refuses 119 firms.
